title: General functional encryption from plain LWE
formal: Does ordinary LWE alone imply public-key functional encryption for arbitrary polynomial-size circuits secure against polynomially many colluding functional-key holders?
definitions: Definitions and model details remain incomplete. Specify selective versus adaptive security, simulation versus indistinguishability, admissible key queries and LWE parameters; bounded collusion is weaker.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of the stated existence or universal proposition, or of its logical negation. This is a provisional candidate, not a completed benchmark specification. context: The supplied catalogue associates this question with Dan Boneh. This is an editorial research connection, not a claim of authorship or a personal research agenda. The candidate retains the bibliography and dated caveats from that catalogue; these have not received a comprehensive independent literature review.
why: This asks whether a central lattice assumption supports general fine-grained access to encrypted data.

import_provenance.original_title: General functional encryption from plain LWE
import_provenance.original_statement: Construct public-key functional encryption for arbitrary polynomial-size circuits, secure against any polynomial number of colluding functional-key holders, from ordinary LWE alone. This is an assumption-focused continuation of Boneh, Sahai and Waters’ general functional-encryption program; bounded-collusion constructions do not meet the target.
